propositions: A one-time backfill script must sample historical commits at configurable cadence (default monthly) and measure cyclomatic complexity and clone-count at each commit.

The script shells to `lizard` for per-function cyclomatic complexity (summed to `complexity` int) and `jscpd` for duplicate block count (`clone_count` int), parsing their JSON/stdout into a `measure_tree(tree_path)` function.
Snapshots written during backfill must be timestamped with the commit's ISO date (from `git show -s --format=%cI`), not wall-clock time, so historical trends are accurately positioned.
If either tool is absent or errors, `measure_tree` returns `None` and that commit is skipped without halting the backfill; all other commits continue to be processed.
All backfilled snapshots are tagged with `source="snapshot"` and `confidence="high"` and routed through the same `snapshot.py` writer as the going-forward path.

Test mocks `measure_tree` to stub tool invocation; it verifies 3 sampled commits yield 3 snapshots with integer `complexity` and `clone_count` keys, correct per-commit `ts`, and proper source/confidence labels.
